title: What does the 6 in 6₁ count?
hook: Knot tables give every knot a number. Is it something you can count in the picture?

knows: a knot is a closed loop of rope, and a drawing shows which strand is on top at each crossing
doesNotKnow: that the first number in a knot's table name, such as 6 in 6₁, is the fewest crossings any drawing of that knot can have, so a drawing can show more crossings than its name says; the second number is only its place in the table

misconception: The number in a knot's name counts something you can see in its drawing, such as the crossings or the loops.
objective: The learner can explain that a knot's name number is the fewest crossings any drawing of it can have, using a drawing that shows more crossings than its name.
keyState: A switched drawing whose crossings drawn differ from its name's first number (milestone 'switched', recorded as {chip, drawn, name}).

claims.text: The first number in a knot's table name is its crossing number: the fewest crossings any drawing of that knot can have ('It is the fewest crossings any drawing of that knot can have'; recall answer 'Some drawing of it has 5 crossings, and none has fewer').
claims.source: Rolfsen, Knots and Links (1976), Appendix C knot table convention (fact-checker to confirm wording); research note company/research/notes/2026-10-13-teachable-knot-theory.md §2.5. Brief claim 1 (company/domains/briefs/math.discrete.md, Knots batch 1 #1). Builder-written; unverified.

claims.text: The kit's 6₁ drawing has 6 crossings and its 5₂ drawing has 5 ('This drawing of 6₁ has 6 crossings'; stage readout 'Crossings drawn: 6 · Name: 6₁' and '5 · 5₂').
claims.source: crossingCount(knot('6_1').pd) = 6 and crossingCount(knot('5_2').pd) = 5 on src/kit/knots; identify returns 6_1 and 5_2. Brief check K1 and K6 (node company/domains/briefs/checks/knots-check.mjs). Builder-written; unverified.

claims.text: 4₁ cannot be drawn with fewer than 4 crossings, and 3₁ with fewer than 3 ('4₁ can be drawn with 4 and never with fewer'; '3₁ can be drawn with 3 and never with fewer').
claims.source: Derivation: the kit's 4_1 and 3_1 drawings are reduced and alternating (simplify status 'minimal', brief check K8; K14 for the switched states). Citation: Tait's first conjecture (a reduced alternating diagram has the fewest crossings), proved 1987 by Kauffman, Murasugi and Thistlethwaite; research note §2.5 (high; full text unchecked). Brief claim 3. Cut first if held (design note cut order). Builder-written; unverified.

claims.text: The second number in a table name is only the knot's place in the table's list among knots with that crossing number ('The number after it is only the knot's place in the table's list').
claims.source: Rolfsen, Knots and Links (1976), Appendix C table convention (fact-checker to confirm). Brief claim 4. Cut second if held (design note cut order). Builder-written; unverified.

claims.text: In the kit's 6₁ drawing, switching any one crossing gives 4₁ (4 of 6) or a plain loop 0₁ (2 of 6); in its 5₂ drawing, a trefoil 3₁ (3 of 5, the mirror image, listed under 3₁) or a plain loop (2 of 5); the drawing keeps 6 (or 5) crossings ('A switch makes a new knot. Yours still had 6 crossings drawn, but its name became 4₁'; stage readout and Seen line).
claims.source: crossingChange, identify and crossingCount on src/kit/knots; brief check K14 (node company/domains/briefs/checks/knots-check.mjs): 6_1 4_1 x4, 0_1 x2; 5_2 3_1* x3, 0_1 x2; pictures keep 6/12 and 5/10 crossings/edges. Builder's node re-run 2026-10-16: 6_1 switches 0,2,3,5 -> 4_1, 1,4 -> 0_1; 5_2 switches 0,2,4 -> 3_1 (mirror), 1,3 -> 0_1. The stage reads identify()[0].name; the mirror flag is not shown. Builder-written; unverified.

claims.text: A plain loop (0₁) can be drawn with no crossings ('its name became 0₁, a plain loop'; 'a plain loop can be drawn with none'; stage 'Name: 0₁, plain loop').
claims.source: The unknot is the round circle, crossing number 0; table entry 0_1 in src/kit/knots (KNOTS['0_1'].c = 0) and Rolfsen's table convention. simplify status 'unknot' for the 0_1 switches (K14). Builder-written; unverified.

claims.text: Knot tables name each knot with a number, and the table draws each knot with the fewest crossings, which is why the kit's 6₁ drawing (and 5₂ drawing) has exactly 6 (and 5) ('Knot tables name each knot with a number, like 6₁'; 'The table draws each knot with that fewest, which is why 6₁ had exactly 6').
claims.source: Rolfsen, Knots and Links (1976), Appendix C: tabulated diagrams are minimal (fact-checker to confirm). Kit: the 6_1 and 5_2 drawings are reduced alternating, simplify status 'minimal', drawn = c (brief checks K1, K6). Builder-written; unverified.

claims.text: Switching a crossing means the strand on top goes under (stage caption 'Switch: top strand goes under').
claims.source: crossingChange in src/kit/knots/index.d.ts ('Switch over/under at crossings'); the standard crossing change. Same caption words as unknot-game (brief W-1569 note). Builder-written; unverified.

recall.question: A drawing of a knot shows 9 crossings. Its table name is 5₂. What follows?
options: Some drawing of it has 5 crossings, and none has fewer
The name is wrong; it should start with 9
Every drawing of it has 9 crossings
recall.why: The first number in a table name is the fewest crossings any drawing of the knot can have. A drawing can show more; the table's own drawing shows the fewest.
